To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) for the Saltzer linear model, the relative fault rate is given by the expression (2n)/(2n-1), where n is the number of sets in a set-associative mapping; (2) for the mixed geometric model, the relative rate is given by (1+1/(2n-1))/[1+1/2(2n-1)]; (3) the dynamic LRU and FIFO mapping algorithms can be shown to have lower miss ratios
the relative performance of set associative mapping algorithms depends on the miss ratio model and that dynamic algorithms are often more effective than static algorithms.

(1) for a given set associativity and miss ratio model, bit selection is the most effective mapping algorithm, (2) the miss ratio of random mapping is within 5% of bit selection, and (3) the miss ratio for FIFO dynamic mapping is within 10% of LRU dynamic mapping.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (a) the development of a theoretical basis for the analysis of set associative page mapping algorithms; (b) the application of this theory to the design of paging algorithms; (c) the use of paging algorithms for cache and main memory; and (d) the use of trace driven simulations to generate results for paging algorithms.
the design and analysis of set associative page mapping algorithms and with the application of these algorithms to cache and main memory.
the analysis of set associative page mapping algorithms for cache and main memory, and with the design of new algorithms that can improve performance over standard bit-selection mapping.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a given miss ratio model, the best mapping algorithm is a dynamic one, and the best static algorithm depends on the miss ratio model.
, given the current state of technology and the cost of memory, set associative paging is a very attractive alternative to fully associative paging.
, for the two miss models we consider, the LRU and FIFO mapping algorithms yield lower fault rates than random or bit-selection paging, but the difference in miss ratio is small.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bit-selection mapping algorithm, although simple, is a poor choice of algorithm for main memory, and that dynamic mapping algorithms should be considered for main memory as well as cache.
the use of bit-selection set associative mapping is a very reasonable choice for cache and main memory paging.
, in the context of a linear model, bit-selection mapping is optimal, while for the mixed-geometric model, bit-selection is suboptimal and dynamic mapping algorithms are superior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dynamic algorithms can yield significantly lower miss rates, and that the miss ratio improvement is not a small constant factor but a significant multiple of the static miss ratio.
the relative fault rates of set associative mapping algorithms can be calculated analytically, and that the dynamic algorithms we suggest may be useful in practice.
, for a given miss ratio, the number of bits required for set associative page mapping can be reduced by 50% relative to fully associative mapping, with only a 10% increase in the miss ratio.
